newsitem.title: CANADA: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA DEFEATS GERMANY, GAINS WORLD SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA DEFEATS GERMANY, GAINS WORLD SEMIFINAL.

text.p: Curtis Joseph stopped 15 shots and Brendan Shanahan scored one power-play goal and set up another as Canada advanced to the semifinals of the World Cup with a 4-1 victory over Germany on Thursday.
Joseph, starting his third game of the tournament, was hardly tested in the final two periods, facing just 11 shots. He has allowed six goals in winning all three of his starts.
Canada, which improved to 3-1, will face Sweden in the semifinals on Saturday in Philadelphia.
"We know the Swedish team has played well, we're looking forward to that game," Canada's Joe Sakic said. "I think we found the format."

Wayne Gretzky of the New York Rangers opened the scoring on the power play with his first goal of the tournament at 3:09 of the first period. He took a pass from Shanahan, who plays for the Hartford Whalers, and blasted a low slapshot past the right pad of goaltender Josef Heiss.
"We're working hard and starting to move the puck," Gretzky said "I think this is a good step to our game against Sweden, but we should've won it by five or six goals."
Canada dominated the opening period, outshooting Germany 17-5, but could only get one shot past Heiss.

Shanahan's power-play tally, his second goal of the tournament, scored at 1:52 into the second period, made it 2-0. Shanahan, left alone to the left of Heiss, took Mark Messier's pass behind the net, wheeled to the front and flipped a backhander between Heiss and the left post.

Germany's lone goal of the contest came 8:34 into the second period. Peter Draisaitl poked the puck away from defenceman Scott Stevens of the New Jersey Devils in the right corner. The puck flipped into the air and Draisaitl batted it over Joseph's left shoulder for his first goal of the tournament.
Trevor Linden of the Vancouver Canucks scored an unassisted goal off a loose puck in the slot with 3:19 left in the middle session for a 3-1 advantage.

Rod Brind'Amour of the Philadelphia Flyers closed the scoring with his first goal of the tournament 3:05 into the final period. He skated around the German defence, moved in on Heiss and lifted a wrist shot past the goaltender's left side.
Heiss stopped 39-of-43 shots as Germany finished the tournament with a 1-3 record.
Only 13,422 fans attended the game, a fact that disappointed Canada's coach Glen Sather.

"I wish people would stop being critical of our team. It isn't easy, this is the 90's," Sather said. "I'm surprised at the small crowd, it's an unusual crowd for a great hockey city. If we were playing in Edmonton, we would've sold the game out."
